architecture.name: overfit-coverage-precedent
architecture.head_dims: The item concerns the verdict on choosing attention-kernel head-dim coverage {64,128} (the SageAttention 2.x set) versus the industry's wider sets. The canonical narrow-set statement: SageAttention maintainer jason-huang03, thu-ml/SageAttention issue #47, 2024-11-24: 'there are difficulities to optmize performance other than 64,128 and 256. For head dim 256 the block size is different so we do not release this for a clean interface (I think head dim greater than 128 is quite rare). For other head dim, we plan to pad it to 64 or 128, just as flash attention does.' Follow-up in the same thread: 'The memory accessing and tensor core computation pattern makes them most suitable for head dim that is a power of 2.' The 2025-2026 d=256 wave retroactively falsified 'rare': Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B (head_dim 256), the entire Qwen3.5 line 0.8B-122B (256), Qwen3.6-27B/35B and Qwen3.8-27B (256), Gemma-2-9B (256), Gemma-3-1B/4B/12B (256), Gemma-4 (256 base + 512 global layers), and Ideogram 4.0 (image generation, 256). All config values verified against official HF config.json files per the sibling head-dim-landscape item (2026-09-06). The falsification is visible ON the original issue: comment by Heliumrich, 2026-06-10: 'Ideogram 4.0 use 256 head_dim, and so Sage Attention 2++ doesn't work :/'. SageAttention CUDA kernels still support only {64,128} as of 2026-09-06.
architecture.qkv_dim_divergence: The {64,128}-style single-dim design also implicitly assumes qk_dim == v_dim. 2025-2026 demand broke that assumption simultaneously: MLA families (DeepSeek-V3/R1, Kimi-K2/K3, GLM-5) run qk 192/256-length keys against v 128/256 with a 512/576 latent cache; llama.cpp added asymmetric DKQ/DV instantiations 192/128 (MiMo-V2.5), 320/256 (Mistral Small 4), 576/512 (DeepSeek/GLM 4.7 Flash, gqa_ratio 20 special-case); FlashInfer's plan API takes head_dim_qk and head_dim_vo separately with the (192,128) pair whitelisted; FA3 allows head_size_v != head_size only on Hopper. SageAttention supports none of these (pad-to-single-dim only, and issues #204 'qk_head_dim = 192 DeepSeek MLA' remains open).
architecture.kv_heads_gqa: Head COUNT (not the overfit axis here, but correlated): GQA is universal in 2025-2026 models (ratios 2:1 to 16:1, e.g. Qwen3.8-27B 24:4, Gemma-4-26B-A4B 16:8, Qwen3-235B 64:4). The relevant interaction: llama.cpp specializes ncols2 (KV columns per Q tile) by GQA ratio per-arch including dedicated Turing branches, i.e. it spends instantiation/specialization budget on BOTH dims and head counts; SageAttention's narrow-dim choice came with no such mechanism, so it could not amortize one narrowing against another axis.
architecture.hybrid_pattern: The d=256 wave coincides with the linear-attention hybrid wave: Qwen3-Next/3.5/3.6/3.8 and Kimi-K3/Kimi-Linear run 3:1 linear:full patterns, so only 25% of layers are full attention - but those layers are exactly the d=256 ones, and a kernel without d=256 blocks the whole model (vLLM gates backends per model, not per layer). Design lesson embedded in the trend: narrowing coverage to 'the common layer' fails when the uncommon layer becomes the gating layer.
architecture.heterogeneous_dims: The strongest aging evidence: Gemma-4-26B-A4B (2026) carries head_dim 256 for sliding-window layers AND a separate global_head_dim 512 for full-attention layers - the first per-layer head-dim heterogeneity in any open model (verified in google/gemma-4-26B-A4B config.json; transformers issue #45201 documents FA2-for-sliding-256 + SDPA-fallback-for-global-512 dispatch because 512 exceeds FA2's max 256). Ecosystem reaction speed: FlashInfer PR #3576 (merged 2026-06-15) added head_dim=512 FA2 paths specifically for 'Gemma4's global (non-sliding window) attention layers' on SM120/121. Coverage sets chosen in 2024 were invalidated within roughly one model generation (~12-18 months).

kernel_support.supported_dims: Coverage sets and stated reasons (mechanisms cross-verified from source in the sibling production-kernel item, 2026-09-06). (1) SageAttention 2.x: strict template whitelist {64,128} in csrc/dispatch_utils.h, error above 128, zero-pad below; STATED REASON (issue #47, 2024-11): perf-difficulty beyond 64/128/256 + belief that >128 is 'quite rare' + power-of-2 tensor-core fit. Narrowest set among surveyed projects. (2) FlashAttention 2: explicit per-hdim instantiation {32,64,96,128,192,256} (generate_kernels.py; flash_fwd_hdim*_sm80.cu files verified on master); STATED REASON (README): 'All head dimensions up to 256' - generality-up-to-a-ceiling bought with instantiation count (6 dims x 2 dtypes x causal/plain x fwd/bwd/split variants); hdim 32 covers small vision towers, 96/192 cover vision-tower dims (e.g. SigLIP/InternViT-class), 256 covers Gemma. (3) llama.cpp fattn: widest set, split MMA path {64,80,96,112,128,256} (V==K) plus asymmetric 192/128, 320/256, 512/512, 576/512 and tile path dkq/dv {40,64,72,80,96,112,128,192,256,320,512,576}; STATED mechanism: model-by-model additions (PR #15769 headsize 256 for Pascal/AMD tile, PR #22286 DKQ=320/DV=256 for Mistral Small 4, PR #26289 tuning head sizes 40-112) with precompiled template-instances/*.cu explicitly to bound compile time - generality via instantiation count plus per-ratio specialization. (4) FlashInfer: DISPATCH_HEAD_DIM {64,128,256,512} in include/flashinfer/utils.cuh; 512 added by PR #3576 (2026-06) for Gemma-4 512-global layers; JIT wrappers cover beyond-AOT dims; the (512,512) AOT entry was later pruned from the default wheel (+~326 MB, commit 54a6156) - a quantified statement of what instantiation generality costs to ship. (5) CUTLASS FMHA (xformers/PyTorch mem-efficient): kMaxK-ceiling template {64, 128, 65536-gmem} instantiated for Sm75 AND Sm80 - generality via a template CEILING instead of per-dim instantiations; kernels skip when head_dim > kMaxK; the kMaxK=65536 gmem-accumulation variant removes the ceiling only for single-iteration (short-KV) cases. Verdict: three distinct generality strategies - instantiating observed dims (FA2, llama.cpp), instantiating a small fixed set on principle (SageAttention), or templating a ceiling (CUTLASS). The projects that chose generality via instantiation count (FA2, llama.cpp) did so because dims are driven by named customer models, not by kernel-author aesthetics; SageAttention's principled narrow set was falsified by exactly that dynamic.
kernel_support.capability_gate: The narrow-set judgment co-evolved with an arch floor: SageAttention's core.py accepts only sm80/86/89/90/120/121 (ValueError otherwise), so its {64,128}-only + '>128 rare' stance was formed entirely on Ampere+ hardware where the models it served were 2024-era d=128 LLMs. FA2 floor sm80 (Turing delegated to ssiu/flash-attention-turing fork); FlashInfer official floor sm80+ with maintainer admission (issue #1648) that sm75 works as an untested subset ('we don't have a SM75 CI machine'); CUTLASS FMHA is the counterexample - explicit Sm75 instantiation made d<=128 generality first-class on Turing; llama.cpp turing_mma_available(cc) makes sm75 first-class including d=256. Lesson: coverage-set decisions made without a Turing (or low-end) axis in view miss that on sm75 the kernel IS the only implementation - there is no faster sibling kernel to fall back to, unlike on sm80+ where a narrow kernel hides behind wide ones.
kernel_support.fallback_semantics: Fallback semantics track coverage philosophy. Narrow-set (SageAttention): throw ValueError 'Unsupported head dim' / pad silently below 128 - failure is loud at the API or subtle in numerics, never graceful. Ceiling-templated (CUTLASS): skip kernel, fall through operator chain (flash -> cutlass -> triton_splitk -> math), ending in NotImplementedError with reasons or PyTorch's silent-slow math backend. Instantiation-wide (llama.cpp): BEST_FATTN_KERNEL_NONE -> op reported unsupported -> backend scheduler picks the non-FA fallback - graceful by construction because coverage is wide enough that fallback is rare. vLLM shows what happens when NO backend covers: Gemma-4 on Turing hits shared-memory limits in every backend (issue #38918) - an error, not a slow path.
kernel_support.ci_hardware_coverage: Coverage claims rot where no sm75 CI exists: FlashInfer broke on SM75 despite README (issue #3620, workaround raised vLLM floor to SM80; fix PR #3621; and a new '[Turing] Restore flashinfer support for SM75' PR #55380 opened 2026-09-04); vLLM's Turing failures (#29743, #38918) are all user-reported, not CI-caught; llama.cpp CUDA CI is compile-only for Turing; FA2/FA3 have zero Turing execution. CUTLASS sm75 kernels at least compile in every PyTorch build. The overfit lesson operationalized: any coverage set wider than what CI exercises is aspirational on legacy hardware.

performance.turing_baseline: Demand-side baseline for Turing-class hardware (2025-2026, no kernel-level perf numbers in this item - those live in the turing-perf items): (1) Cloud pricing per Modal's 'How much does it cost to run NVIDIA T4 GPUs in 2025?' - T4 at $0.59/hr on Modal ($0.000164/s serverless), AWS G4dn $0.526/hr, Azure NCasT4_v3 $0.526/hr, GCP $0.35/hr on-demand ($0.14 spot), Vast.ai ~$0.151/hr; Modal calls the T4 'the lowest entry price for GPU compute across major cloud providers' and a 'workhorse GPU for AI inference in 2025'. (2) Used market: ~$250 is in line with 2025 eBay US pricing for used T4s [uncertain - approximate community/eBay figure; the Modal article itself quotes $845 NEW (Amazon PNY listing) and does not give a used price]. (3) Free tier: the T4 remained Google Colab's standard free GPU in 2025 (12h sessions, availability not guaranteed, cooldowns commonly 2-4h) - i.e. the GPU most first-time and student users touch is sm75. (4) Ollama officially lists Turing (7.5, T4, RTX 20-series) among supported architectures: 'Ollama supports Nvidia GPUs with compute capability 5.0+ and driver version 550 and newer' with CC 5.0-6.2 requiring driver 570+ (docs.ollama.com/gpu) - Turing sits mid-range in Ollama's support window, not at its edge. (5) AWS G4dn/G4ad remain the default budget inference instance families built on T4/INFERENTIA-era Turing silicon.
performance.d256_feasibility: Is the falsifying dimension achievable on the hardware in question? On sm75: YES, proven in production by llama.cpp - MMA path instantiates DKQ=DV=256 with Turing-specific ncols2=32 scheduling branches, and the tile path runs dkq256-dv256 (PR #15769) by chunking DKQ across smem stages; the 576/512 MLA case runs on Turing behind a KV-length-tuned branch. On sm80+: FA2 hdim256 instantiated, sitting exactly at the smem boundary (launch template requires max_smem_per_block >= 2*headdim*(128+2*64) ~ 128 KiB for the large-tile shape; Ampere's 164 KiB fits, Turing's 64 KiB does not). Contrast case: vLLM #38918 shows every stock vLLM backend exhausting shared memory on Turing with Gemma-4's 256-class dims - the difference between llama.cpp's hand-tuned Turing chunking and generic autotuned kernels is the difference between feasible and blocked.
performance.cost_analysis: Quantified cost of choosing generality vs overfitting. First, instantiation count: FA2 = 6 hdims x 2 dtypes x plain/causal x {fwd, bwd, split, split_align} generated files; FA3 splits per-hdim .cu files (hdim x dtype x softcap x arch) to parallelize nvcc; llama.cpp precompiles template-instances/fattn-*-instance-*.cu expressly to bound compile time; SageAttention's 2-dim set is the cheapest to build but pushes all out-of-set demand to error/padding. Second, wheel and binary cost: FlashInfer's single (512,512) FA2 AOT entry added ~326 MB wheel size (commit 54a6156) and was pruned to JIT-only - the canonical datapoint that high-dim instantiation is expensive to DISTRIBUTE even when cheap to compile once. Third, padding cost (the narrow-set alternative): 96->128 zero-pad adds ~33% wasted K-loop work and perturbs quantization statistics (SageAttention pads all of q/k/v); padding cannot reach 256 from 128 at all (>128 is out of range), so the narrow-set strategy has NO answer to the d=256 wave. Finally, chunking cost (the middle path): llama.cpp nbatch_K/nbatch_V chunk tables per arch let 256/320/576 run on 64 KiB-smem Turing at some accumulation-reordering cost - generality purchased with kernel complexity rather than instantiation count.

design_fit.route: Informs all three sm_75 bridge routes. Route A (native d=256 template): the precedent says 256 is mandatory, and llama.cpp's Turing MMA 256/256 instance is the existence proof. Route B (k-chunked 256 on a 128-wide pipeline): the precedent's chunking cost analysis (nbatch_K tables, accumulation reorder) is the price of Route B; chunking also extends to 512 for Gemma-4 globals. Route C (bridge-header completeness for unmodified FA2/FlashInfer): a bridge claiming to substitute for FA2/FlashInfer must claim at least {64,128,256} (FA2's Turing-relevant set capped at its 256 API ceiling) and ideally the FlashInfer set {64,128,256,512}; claiming only {64,128} would reproduce the SageAttention failure mode in a market where that failure is already documented.
design_fit.recommendation: Design lessons maintainers should draw, concretely for the sm_75 bridge kernel plan: (1) Treat the SageAttention #47 statement as the canonical cautionary artifact: a coverage-set judgment anchored on 'current models' aged in ~12 months; anchor instead on the observed 2025-2026 set {64,128,256} + a chunked path to 512. (2) Buy generality the way FA2/llama.cpp did - instantiation count bounded by template-instance files - not the SageAttention way; the marginal dim costs compile time, not correctness. (3) Reserve ceiling-templating (CUTLASS kMaxK style) for the fallback/generic path, and be explicit that its gmem variant only covers short-KV. (4) Publish a per-dim smem feasibility table up front and decline unsupported dims explicitly (llama.cpp-style graceful unsupported op), because the alternative - vLLM #38918's all-backends-exhaust-smem - is the worst user outcome. (5) Assume one-generation aging: design the dispatch so adding 512 (or asymmetric 192/128) is a new instantiation entry, not a redesign. (6) Stand up a T4/2080Ti CI runner: every rot incident found (FlashInfer #3620, vLLM #38918/#29743) traces to zero sm75 CI.
design_fit.numerics_risks: Correctness risks tied to the coverage decision: (1) d=256 accumulation order - QK^T over 256-wide heads doubles the fp32 accumulation chain vs 128, and chunked (Route B) vs native (Route A) implementations reorder it, so bit-exactness claims must be per-route; llama.cpp documents overflow risk in low-precision accumulate paths (Q pre-scaled 0.25 in tile kernel) - directly relevant to Turing fp16-accumulate mma. (2) Softcap - Gemma-2/3/4 logit softcapping must be applied pre-softmax; llama.cpp compiles softcap only for specific DV values (128/256/512), i.e. coverage sets and numerics features are coupled - a dim covered without its numerics feature is a silent-wrongness trap. (3) bf16 absent on Turing (vLLM #29743 log: 'doesn't support torch.bfloat16. Falling back to torch.float16'), so 2025-2026 bf16-native models on sm75 run fp16 with range/precision drift. (4) SageAttention's own bug history (#386 int32 overflow silently corrupting outputs, #392 silently-wrong output on CUDA-graph replay) shows narrow-set projects also carry quantization-specific silent risks; padding-induced changes to per-channel quant statistics are an additional hazard of the pad-to-128 strategy.
design_fit.demand_weighting: Who is actually blocked by missing d=256 (and >128 generally) on sm_75: (1) Installed base - the T4 is the cheapest cloud GPU across major providers (Modal $0.59/hr, AWS G4dn $0.526/hr, GCP $0.35/hr, Vast.ai $0.151/hr), the standard free Colab GPU, ~$250 used on eBay [uncertain - approximate], and officially supported mid-range in Ollama (CC 5.0+ window lists Turing explicitly); FlashInfer #1648: 'Tesla T4 and the RTX 20xx series are still the most common GPUs in the market'. (2) Concrete blockage: vLLM #29743 (2025-11-30, T4G user): Qwen3-VL 'there is no supported backend for Turing GPUs (SM75, e.g., T4 and T4G)' - FLASH_ATTN requires sm80, FlashInfer/Triton paths incomplete for the model's attention, TORCH_SDPA deregistered; closed 'not planned' - i.e. the flagship open-model family is officially unrunnable on the largest cheap-GPU base in the highest-distribution inference framework. Companion evidence: vLLM #7464 (Gemma-2 on T4, 2024-08), #38918 (Gemma-4 on Turing: every backend hits smem limits, 2026-04), #8929 (xformers lacks Gemma-2 softcap), open PRs #55380 '[Turing] Restore flashinfer support for SM75' (2026-09) and #49077 (TRITON_ATTN fp8 KV on SM75) showing maintainer/patch-level demand persists. (3) Model distribution - d=256 full-attention layers now span the highest-distribution open families (Qwen3.5/3.6/3.8 whole line, Gemma-2/3/4) plus image generation (Ideogram 4.0, per SageAttention #47 comment) and heterogeneous 512 globals (Gemma-4-26B-A4B), while d=128 remains the 2023-2025 installed base and GPT-OSS is the lone d=64 family: a {64,128,256(+512-chunked)} set covers essentially all of it; {64,128} covers only the legacy slice. (4) Who is NOT blocked: llama.cpp users (Turing d=256 MMA/tile shipped), PyTorch/xformers CUTLASS users up to d<=128 (+short-KV gmem). Net: on Turing the framework that took the narrow-set position (SageAttention sm80 floor) and the framework that refused the feature (vLLM closing #29743 not-planned) ceded the entire d=256-on-Turing population to llama.cpp.
design_fit.academic_grounding: Does theory predict >128 head dims keep growing? Mixed. (1) Bhojanapalli et al., 'Low-Rank Bottleneck in Multi-head Attention Models', ICML 2020 (arXiv:2002.07028, ~187 citations): attention head rank is bounded by min(head_size, sequence_length, embedding_dim); the low-rank bottleneck appears because current architectures fix head size (~64/128) regardless of context length; their fixup - set head size at least the sequence length - is impractical at modern context lengths, but the paper predicts upward pressure on head size as contexts grow, which is consistent with 128->256 arriving alongside the long-context era. (2) 'The Effect of Attention Head Count on Transformer Approximation' (arXiv:2510.06662, v1 2025-10-08, v2 2026-03-31, accepted ICLR 2026): provable bounds - with too FEW heads, parameter count must blow up exponentially (O(1/eps^(cT))) for approximation; sufficient heads make approximation efficient. This pressures MORE heads (and hence, at fixed hidden size, SMALLER head dims) - the opposite direction. (3) 'Leaner Transformers: More Heads, Less Depth' (arXiv:2505.20802, 2025-05-27, Saratchandran/Teney/Lucey): multi-head attention's benefit is conditioning of the attention block, not per-head capacity; more, smaller heads with reduced depth cut parameters 30-50% at equal accuracy - again anti-head-size-growth. Net academic read: theory gives a lower bound pressure on head DIM only via the rank/sequence-length argument (and GQA pushes KV dims down); the observed 128->256 move is better explained by engineering conventions (hidden_size/num_heads at scale, RoPE partitioning, KV-cache economics) than by approximation theory - reinforcing that kernel coverage sets should be driven by ecosystem observation (instantiation of observed dims) rather than by either theory or one-time frequency judgments.
